newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks close off highs after strong start.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks close off highs after strong start.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur stocks closed off their session highs as heavyweight blue-chips also retreated.

Tenaga's fortunes rose and fell on news that the company would be compensating consumers for an August 3 nationwide power outage, after all. The stock closed unchanged at 9.30, after reaching a high of 9.85 in morning trading. It was the day's second-most actively traded stock with 4.3 million shares changing hands.
The blue-chip Composite Index closed up 0.43 points to 1156.83 after reaching an intra-day high of 1163.00
The Second Board index added 5.13 points to 604.96.
"There has been some institutional buying today, especially on Maybank and United Engineers," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas.

"Fund managers have been overweight on Kuala Lumpur, but have nonetheless been worried over the country's current account deficit. But now with the latest trade surplus, they can see that we are able to manage the economy," added Tan.
Volume was slightly lower than that on Tuesday, with 237 million shares traded, valued at 2,008 million ringgit. Gainers led losers 303 to 250.
"The movements on Tenaga have been very much sentiment-driven," said Alex Tan, head of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"Even if the final quantum of the compensation they have to pay is around 150 million ringgit, this is still only around three to four percent of their 1997 net earnings. There are no fundamentals on the volatility of the stock," he added.
Equities dealers and analysts said they were now more bullish about the prospects of the stock market after the release of better-than-expected trade figures.
Sime Darby was once again in the most actives list. the stock closed up five cents at 8.65. "This is a liquidity-driven, traditional blue-chip stock, which still has some spice to it," said Tan.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot October contract traded down four points to close at 1156.0 with 387 lots traded, while the November contract was down 5.5 points, settling at 1159.0 with 16 lots traded.
